senses.definition: (computing, of a resource) Connected directly to a particular computer, processor, etc.; able to be accessed offline.
examples: The panel shows both local and remote sites.

senses.definition: (computing, of a variable or identifier) Having limited scope (either lexical or dynamic); only accessible within a certain portion of a program.
(mathematics, not comparable, of a condition or property) Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as "near points;" in particular:

subsenses.definition: (topology) Satisfied by at least one open neighborhood of every point.
examples: A Hausdorff space satisfying local compactness need not be (globally) compact!

subsenses.definition: (topology) Satisfied by arbitrarily small open neighborhoods of every point.
(group theory, of a property of an infinite group) Satisfied by every finitely generated subgroup.

senses.definition: (mathematics, not comparable, of a condition or property) Detectable from the behavior of substructures understood to be "near points;" in particular:

subsenses.definition: (algebra, algebraic geometry, of a property P of a ring R (or an R-module M)) Such that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) P holds for R (M); (2) P holds for the localization R_p (M_p) for all prime ideals p of R; (3) P holds for the localization R_m (M_m) for all maximal ideals m of R.
(group theory, of a property of a finite group) Detectable from the behavior of the normalizers of the nontrivial p-subgroups.

senses.definition: (algebra, of a ring) Having a unique maximal (left) ideal.
(medicine) Of or pertaining to a restricted part of an organism.
examples: The patient didn't want to be sedated, so we applied only local anesthesia.
Hawaiian Pidgin is spoken by the local population.

senses.definition: A person who lives in or near a given place.
examples: It's easy to tell the locals from the tourists.

quotes.text: Taunton station is busy - even more so when the inbound working of my Bristol train arrives, laden with the usual mix of 'staycationers' and locals.
